findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed carrots stored below raw fish in the prep cooler. CORRECTED- carrots were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Ensure ready to eat food are always stored ABOVE raw foods to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: PIC began to don gloves after handling a cellphone without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the behavior and reminded PIC to wash hands, which they did, then donned gloves to continue work. Ensure employees wash hands after any task that may have contaminated them and before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink was observed blocked by a roll of plastic wrap upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- PIC moved the plastic wrap so the handsink is accessible. Keep handsinks clear and accessible at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: There is no ambient thermometer present inside of the bottom of the prep cooler. Ensure thermometers are provided inside all cold holding units (in addition to any digital thermometers that may be built in to the units).
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: A sealed package of ROP tuna was observed thawed in the bottom of the sushi prep cooler. The package had written instructions to remove from packaging before thawing. Upon request, PIC cut the package and removed the thawed fish. Ensure ROP fish is thawed according to the supplier’s instructions.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
One of the two employees present has not completed food handler training. Ensure all employees who handle food or wash dishes complete food handler training within 30 days of hire. Keep food handler certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee began to don gloves after handling their phone without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee, who then washed hands and donned gloves. Wash hands before donning gloves and after any activity that may have contaminated hands.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not setup for use. PIC provided quat solution during inspection. Ensure sanitizer solution is setup and available for use prior to beginning food preparation and packaging. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Freshly prepared sushi products were placed directly in the display case and were not properly cooled to 41F/below in the walk-in freezer or walk-in cooler as required by the FujiSan HACCP plan. Internal temperatures were observed above 50F for products placed in the display case after morning prep. Spicy California rolls that were getting packaged in the prep room were observed with internal temperatures of 57F-61F. All products prepared as of this morning were taken to the walk-in freezer to allow for proper chilling before being placed back in the display case. 
The pH for sushi rice prepared this morning was not documented in the Managers Red Book (daily HACCP documentation log). PIC at time of inspection stated the pH meter was calibrated and used this morning to verify proper pH of rice. When asked to demonstrate calibration of pH meter and show pH of sushi rice, the pH meter would not stabilize at 4.0 for buffer solution. PIC stated the pH meter currently in use is new, and PIC was unsure as to what might be wrong with it. Inspector will return on 2/1/22 when manager is back from training to verify proper function of pH meter.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC changed gloves without washing hands. Handwashing between glove changes was discussed. PIC was observed washing hands as needed for remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Ice water used for calibration of food thermometer was discarded in the handwashing sink. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed. Ensure the handwashing sink if not used as a dump sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) 1. PIC handled wallet with gloved hands when getting out their manager certification card. Gloves were not removed prior to approaching prep area to continue food handling. PIC was advised on proper glove use. Gloves were discarded and hands washed prior to PIC putting on a new pair of gloves. 
2. The other person helping with prep was observed touching their face mask with gloved hands. PIC was advised to ensure gloves are changed between tasks and after face masks are touched or adjusted. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Freshly prepared sushi products placed directly in the display case had internal temperatures above 50F. California rolls were observed at 57F. All products prepared this morning were moved to the walk-in freezer to quickly chill to proper temperature. Packaged products were moved back to the display case after reaching internal temperatures of 30F-33F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Facility manager has been documenting calibration of the food thermometer daily for the past 2 weeks but confirmed the food thermometer was not getting checked as required by company HACCP plan. Manager was unsure where to get ice for calibration. Manager got ice from the cafe at the request of inspector and was able to confirm calibration at 32F during inspection. Manager was advised to follow the FujiSan HACCP requirements and make sure calibration of the food thermometer occurs daily along with calibration of the pH meter prior to use. Documentation should not be made otherwise if calibration hasn’t occurred as that is falsifying documents. 
Manager has also been documenting time for acidified rice at 6am when calibration of pH meter is being documented at 7am. Manager confirmed the time in the log was when the rice finished cooking prior to adding rice vinegar after calibration of the pH meter. Time when rice is acidified needs to be documented. Manager stated he understood and will change his practice to allow for proper documentation.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sanitizer-bucket was at 100ppm. Solution was prepared upon arrival of manager early this morning. Fresh sanitizer solution was prepared at 200ppm. Manager was advised to change the solution throughout operations daily as needed based on use.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged Ahi tuna steaks and salmon were observed in the walkin cooler. Manager stated the packages are not opened until product is needed and noted the products in question would be used within the next two days. Directions on the packaging states to open the package and thaw under refrigeration immediately before use. Manager was advised on proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish. Ensure vacuum packaged frozen fish are removed from the package and thawed in a covered pan under refrigeration or at minimum the packaging is opened to eliminate the reduced oxygen environment. Follow the directions on packaging when thawing any portions of vacuum packaged fish. **See general comments for additional information**
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, its thawing using cold running water as specified in the 2017 FDA Food Code.
